findings.finding: Selected beat H51-03 (Mark 1:14–15, after the Baptist is delivered up) currently precedes H52-01 (John 1:35–51, where the Baptist is standing with two disciples). A continuous narrative without an explicit retrospective step gives the wrong temporal inference.
findings.candidateSupplement: John 1:29–34 as a possible retrospective link to John 1:35; source scene 071 is not itself in selected P3 reading
findings.requiredNextReview: Validate within-Gospel timeline and oral continuity with named Challoner/Crampon witnesses; only then edit P3 owner.

findings.finding: The existing title promises teaching and signs, but the chosen Scripture beats are the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:1–12) and Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:9–15). The healing of the paralytic is context-only, not a selected Scripture beat.
findings.alternativeRequiresSourceSelection: Keep existing title only if at least one sign is selected with its own verse witness and editorially costed abridgment
findings.requiredNextReview: Editorially decide accuracy of title vs explicit sign selection; do not show context-only story as original Scripture.

findings.finding: John 6:26–35 is followed directly by 47–59. The omitted 36–46 contains disbelief, the Father's will, Jewish objections and the Father's drawing (notably 6:41–45), so the progression is not merely a short repetition. The linked scene 097's Capernaum synagogue sentence is at verse 60 in current English witnesses but 59 in French.
findings.proposedTextualSeamToEvaluate: John 6:36–46; assess whether a shorter context-preserving sequence can be justified without losing verse 44/45
findings.distinctSignContext: John 6:1–15 loaves remain separate from this discourse; H56-01 is editorial context, not scripture
findings.requiredNextReview: Compare every verse of 26–60 against named English/French printed witnesses; establish an edition-aware bilingual display, then perform theology and oral review.

findings.finding: The selected Matthew 16:13–28 and Matthew 17:1–9 provide the confession, Passion prediction and six-day Transfiguration transition within one Gospel witness. No passage gap requires fabricated narrative, but those are three distinct visual beats.
findings.requiredNextReview: Source compare, oral read, 3 distinct artwork subjects and qualified Tabor label; no new geographical point.

findings.finding: The selected John 11:20–27 describes Martha and explicitly says Mary remained at home. Jumping to 11:32–35 makes Mary appear before Christ without the 11:28–31 summons and movement; her agency and the mourners' reaction are lost.
findings.proposedTextualSeamToEvaluate: Insert John 11:28–31 or minimally 11:28–29 between selected 11:20–27 and 11:32–35
findings.heldPlotBridge: HS-CF-05 (John 11:45–53) remains candidate and must not be automatically appended
findings.requiredNextReview: Review the continuous 11:1–44 narrative, compare Catholic witnesses, weigh smallest adequate bridge and only then alter P3 source selections.
